newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK March producer price data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK March producer price data.

text.p: Following is a list of analysts' reactions to UK March producer price data published at 0830 GMT.
(Expectations input +0.2% s/a m/m, -6.5% unadj y/y; output +0.1% m/m, +1.2% y/y; output ex food, drink and tobacco +0.1% m/m, +0.5% y/y)
* UK MARCH OUTPUT PRICES -0.1% MM,+1.0% YY, INPUT PRICES -7.6% YY,S/A -0.5% MM
* UK MARCH S/A OUTPUT PRICES EX F,D,T,P +0.1% MM, +0.5% YY
* UK MARCH S/A OUTPUT PRICES EX F,D,T,P +0.1% 3M/3M +0.2% 3M VS SAME YR AGO.

CHRIS TINKER, CHIEF TREASURY ECONOMIST STANDARD CHARTERED - "The overall balance of the numbers has come in .... at the positive end of any expectations certainly in terms of these import numbers, clearly oil price related."
"But we must bear in mind that the impact that input prices actually have into the overall RPI is actually limited.
We do have average earnings numbers coming out on Wednesday which I think will keep too much expectation of an improvement in sentiment in check.

Nevertheless the headlines particularly in terms and this astonishing input number will allow the authorities to highlight that inflation is just not an issue we should be worrying about at this stage," Tinker said.

BANK OF AMERICA ECONOMIST JEREMY HAWKINS - "The UK PPIs are at the softer end of expectations and should dampen speculation that the expected hike after the election will be as much as 50 basis points.

"Core output prices - the most important single release - are up just 0.5% on the year. Suggests that competitiveness factors are still a major feature in which case, while not well correlated on a month basis, the PPIs bode well for Thursday's RPIs. We still expect base rate to be hiked 25 bps after the election and until such time, upside to UK asset markets will be limited.

DAVID PHILPOTTS, Schroders economist- "The point that we shouldn't miss is that any inflation that is likely to build up in the UK this year and particularly next is likely to come more from the Labour party rather than the goods market.
In fact we'll see a very similar picture to what we're seeing in the U.S. at the moment. It may well be that the authrities are raising rate because they're worried about wage pressures picking up."
